purpose: Define each query, ingest, mutation, federation, migration, replication or maintenance execution as belonging to an explicit workload identity/profile separate from the operation and execution identities themselves.

topics.name: DWH Workload Identity
topics.purpose: Define each query, ingest, mutation, federation, migration, replication or maintenance execution as belonging to an explicit workload identity/profile separate from the operation and execution identities themselves.

semantics.identity_rule: Every managed workload/profile has an explicit identity.
semantics.execution_rule: Concrete executions reference workload identity but keep their own execution identities.
semantics.scope_rule: Workload may bind exact instance/project/user/service/profile scopes.
semantics.resource_rule: Workload resource constraints are explicit and separate from semantic operation definitions.
semantics.priority_rule: Priority is scheduling metadata and never semantic business priority unless separately modeled.
semantics.authority_rule: Workload classification does not grant operation/data authority.
semantics.path_rule: Queue name/process id/thread id is not canonical workload identity.

invariants.rule: Admission, quotas, concurrency, priority, cancellation and resource budgets may control when/how work executes but never change canonical query/write semantics, data ownership, classification or authorization.

hard_gates.condition: queue name used as semantic workload identity
workload identity replaces query/write execution identity

references.purpose: Query executions may participate in managed workloads.
Mutation executions retain exact operation identity.

prose.summary: Define each query, ingest, mutation, federation, migration, replication or maintenance execution as belonging to an explicit workload identity/profile separate from the operation and execution identities themselves.
